strengths: Addresses a relevant NLP reliability problem: recognizing missing or contradictory information in mathematical word problems. Paired perturbations of four established datasets provide a useful diagnostic setting.

The core design is coherent: represent unknown quantities explicitly, check satisfiability, and test uniqueness of the requested answer. These checks are appropriate when the generated constraints faithfully represent the problem.

Experiments cover two LLM backbones and show large reported gains in contradiction rejection. With GPT-4, SLP achieves 80.52–86.00%, while the listed baselines reach at most 14.43%. Prompt-sensitivity experiments and extensive example prompts provide additional diagnostic material.
weaknesses: The aggregate evaluation conflicts with its definition. Under Equation (2), well-defined accuracy above 50% guarantees a positive score because ill-defined items contribute nonnegative values. Yet Table 2 reports PAL/AddSub accuracy of 95.95% and an AddSub-C R-Score of -3.67. The authors must reconcile the equation and tables, explain normalization, and provide outcome counts and rules for identifying rejection and handling execution failures.

The comparison confounds method with demonstration content. SLP receives four solvable, two missing-condition, and two contradictory examples; the main few-shot baselines receive solvable examples. The published CoT-X/PAL-X examples lack comparable contradiction demonstrations. Moreover, PAL-8 incorrectly rejects solvable questions with answers 20-12 and 32+42 (Appendix D.6), undermining the trade-off analysis. Corrected comparisons using matched demonstrations are necessary.

The claimed verification mechanism depends on unverified semantic translation. In Appendix C.4, the robe encoding omits blue_fiber == 2, making its constraints satisfiable with multiple answers despite the claimed contradiction detection. Appendix D.1 also sets Monday-to-Thursday total_days == 0. These substantive errors warrant an audit separating faithful formalizations, incorrect constraints, and execution failures; binary rejection alone does not establish correct recognition.

Benchmark diversity and validation are insufficiently established. Every contradiction uses one appended conditional template, which also appears in SLP demonstrations. There are no matched satisfiable conditional controls or held-out contradiction templates to exclude reliance on surface cues. The construction process lacks independent label-audit results, detailed annotation procedures, and generation/verification prompts; data and code release are only promised.

The claim that SLP escapes the reasoning/rejection trade-off exceeds the evidence. For example, GPT-3.5 MultiArith accuracy is 86.50% for SLP versus 98.17% for PAL. False-rejection rates and controlled comparisons are needed to characterize this cost. The promising contribution requires corrected scoring, repaired prompts, and experimental reruns before Findings-level soundness and reproducibility are established, supporting resubmission next cycle.
